scope: IMP-02 line 327: write a durable pre-update inventory before the package-manager updater runs
status: implemented-with-isolated-fixtures; no real manager was updated

reviewFindings.reusedInfrastructure: Followed the existing ownership journal conventions: schema version field, deny_unknown_fields, a reparse-component check before writing, and write-then-rename.
reviewFindings.scopeDecided: These managers expose no supported way to reinstall an exact previous version, so a real rollback plan cannot be built. The honest deliverable is an audit trail written before the command runs, plus an explicit statement that it is not a rollback.

implementation.recordShape: UpdateRecord { status, tool, executablePath, beforeVersion, afterVersion, program, arguments, attempt }
lifecycle: record_planned is written before the updater runs; if it cannot be written the update is cancelled rather than run unaudited
record_outcome attaches the result to the exact attempt token; completed / unverified / failed are distinct
an unknown or already-settled attempt token is an error, never a silent no-op
implementation.whyAttemptToken: Without it, two overlapping updates of the same manager could settle the wrong record. The token is generated per call and matched on update.
implementation.unverifiedIsItsOwnState: A command that exited 0 but whose version could not be read is recorded as unverified, not as success.
implementation.bounds: MAX_RECORDS = 50; the oldest records are dropped first.
implementation.refusesRedirectedJournal: A junction or symlink at the journal path is refused before any write, so the record cannot be redirected outside the backups directory.
implementation.failureVisibility: If settling the record fails after the command ran, the error is attached to the returned result instead of being swallowed.

ui.command: node tests/run-ui.mjs <global playwright module> 九套测试

notVerified: No real package manager was updated, so no real journal was produced by the production command path; the module is exercised directly and the wiring is compile-checked.
Crash-during-update was simulated by leaving a record in the planned state, not by killing a real process.
The journal is not surfaced anywhere in the UI yet.
limitations: This is an audit trail, not a rollback: there is no supported command to return to the recorded previous version.
The record is pruned at 50 entries, so an older attempt can disappear.
The journal records what was about to run; it cannot prove the updater did what it claimed.
